audit_notes: Model: same exponentially graded layer as the dolphin-skin elite, G(z) = G_base exp(k z), k = ln(6e4/3e6) = -3.91, loaded at the surface by a fluctuation amplitude p'_rms = 45 Pa (treated as a quasi-static shear traction). Analytical: surface compliance C = u(1)/p' = (t/G_base)(e^{3.91}-1)/3.91 = 1e-9*12.5 = 1.25e-8 m/Pa. Drag check (not computable by the steady model, done here by energy balance): dissipated power per area P = pi*tan_delta*p'^2*C*f = 3.14*1*2025*1.25e-8*300 = 0.024 W/m2, compared with near-wall turbulence production ~ tau*U ~ 126 W/m2, i.e. 0.02%; the drag benefit claimed (0.5%) would need a leverage of ~25 of dissipated energy on turbulent production, for which there is no evidence. I rate the direct drag effect as ~0-0.2%. Metric chosen for what the field shows: fouling detachment stress sigma_c = sqrt(2 w_a/C) versus a standard silicone foul-release coating (t = 0.3 mm, homogeneous G = 0.33 MPa, C = 9.1e-10 m/Pa): expected sigma_c ratio 0.27, i.e. ~73% lower. This is a release gain, not a drag gain. Stability: G_surface = 6e4 Pa gives c_s = sqrt(6e4/1100) = 7.4 m/s, practically equal to the cruising speed 7 m/s; U/c_s = 0.95 is in the range where compliant layers develop hydroelastic surface waves (static divergence reported for U above ~1-2 c_s). This is a serious risk: I keep the audit passed because the parameters are within physical limits, but the surface modulus is at the edge of the safe range, and a tan_delta ~ 1 gel has low tear strength (<1 kN/m) and poor abrasion resistance. Hydrolytic stability of silicone gels is good. Dimensionless: U/c_s = 0.95, modulus ratio 0.02, dissipation share 2e-4, surface strain p'/G = 7.5e-4.

independent_var.label: Normalized depth from primer (0) to surface (1)

performance_gain.label: Reduction of fouling detachment stress vs standard foul-release coating

hard_constraints: surface_shear_modulus >= 5e4 Pa; U/c_s < 1 at design speed

baseline_description: Standard clean silicone foul-release coating, 0.3 mm, homogeneous E ~ 1 MPa
